Run tree-based soft gating on a SpatialExperiment

Source: R/run_pipeline.R
run_tree_gating.Rd

Build a marker-based, hierarchical soft-gating model for each lineage in a marker table, compute per-cell membership probabilities, and derive hard lineage/state labels.

Usage

run_tree_gating(
  spe,
  lineage_table,
  assay_name = "exprs",
  max_depth = 4,
  min_cells = 200,
  min_score = 0.5,
  uncert_thresh = 0.25,
  neg_strength = 0.4,
  cutoff_method = c("mean", "equal_posteriors"),
  gmm_model_names = NULL,
  workers = 1
)

Arguments

spe

A SpatialExperiment or SingleCellExperiment containing per-cell marker expression.

lineage_table

A data.frame/tibble with at least the columns cell_type, pos_markers, and neg_markers. Marker columns must be list-columns of character vectors. Markers not present in spe are dropped during cleaning.

assay_name

Character scalar naming the assay in spe used as the expression matrix (default "exprs").

max_depth

Integer; maximum recursion depth of each gating tree.

min_cells

Integer; minimum number of cells required to allow a node split.

min_score

Numeric; minimum separability score required to accept a split.

uncert_thresh

Numeric in [0,1]; cells whose best (non-proliferating) lineage probability is below this threshold are labeled "Uncertain".

neg_strength

Numeric in [0,1]; strength of the negative-marker penalty applied within tree_prob() (default 0.4). Larger values increase the penalty from negative-marker expression.

cutoff_method

Cutoff selection method passed to fit_gmm_2(). One of "mean" or "equal_posteriors".

gmm_model_names

Optional character vector of model names to pass to mclust::Mclust() for 1D GMM fitting (e.g., "V", "E"). Use NULL (default) to allow selection by BIC.

workers

Optional integer number of workers for parallel execution. Defaults to 1.

Value

A named list with components:

spe

The input spe with added colData columns: P_* (per-lineage probabilities), cell_type_hard, cell_type_state, prob_best, and prob_prolif.

trees

A named list of fitted gating trees, one per cell_type.

prob_mat

Numeric matrix of per-cell probabilities (cells \(\times\) cell types).

hard_label

Character vector of hard lineage labels after applying uncert_thresh.

lineage_table

The cleaned marker table actually used to build the trees.

Details

For each cell_type in lineage_table, a gating tree is fit from positive and (optionally) negative marker sets. Per-cell probabilities are then computed by evaluating each fitted tree via tree_prob(), with an optional negative-marker penalty controlled by neg_strength.

Hard labels are assigned as the lineage with the highest probability (excluding "Proliferating"), unless the best probability is below uncert_thresh, in which case the cell is labeled "Uncertain". If a "Proliferating" lineage is present, cells with proliferating probability \(\ge 0.5\) and not "Uncertain" receive a "Prolif " prefix in cell_type_state.

Marker statistics used for logistic scoring/penalization are precomputed once across all markers appearing in lineage_table via fit_marker_stats(). Trees are built with build_fullcoverage_tree() and evaluated with tree_prob().

Examples

### This is a minimal example, for the full example, please see vignettes
data("cytoGateR_example", package = "cytoGateR")
image_ids <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(cytoGateR_example)$image_name
spe <- cytoGateR_example[, image_ids == image_ids[1L]]
lineage_table <- data.frame(
  cell_type = c("Tcell", "Bcell"),
  pos_markers = I(list("CD3e", "CD20")),
  neg_markers = I(list("CD20", "CD3e"))
)
tree_result <- run_tree_gating(
  spe,
  lineage_table,
  max_depth = 1,
  min_cells = 100,
  min_score = 0.1,
  workers = 1
)
#> Building 1th tree - Tcell Cell Type.
#> finished tree 1 - Tcell | elapsed: 0.052 s | peak RAM: 0.02 GB
#> Building 2th tree - Bcell Cell Type.
#> finished tree 2 - Bcell | elapsed: 0.031 s | peak RAM: 0.02 GB
head(tree_result$hard_label)
#> [1] "Uncertain" "Uncertain" "Uncertain" "Uncertain" "Uncertain" "Tcell"
